findings.claim: O2 says `needs: none`, but its check reads lifecycle badges that O1 creates. O2's check is that kmaudit's lifecycle badge says beta and kmctl's says stable, and O1 is the outcome that adds those badges to all three READMEs. Eval r2 also asks that every earlier README test passes, which assumes r1 has landed. Both outcomes also edit the same four files (README.md, the kmaudit README and tests/test_readmes.py). If plan.split trusts `needs: none` and runs them as two independent tickets, either O2 has no badge to check, or both tickets add the same badge and collide. Fix one of two ways: give O2 `needs: O1`, or move the lifecycle badge out of O1 into O2 so O1 covers only CI, release, licence and Python, then align r1 and r2 to match.
